name: Oregon Women's Land Trust
notes: Owl Farm (OWL) is the trust's land: in 1983 OWLT was "in the process of buying OWL FARM" (per LC Mar/Apr 1983). The 145 acres OWLT "has bought" in 1976 are probably the same land as Owl Farm's 147 acres, but no listing says so.

name: Four Women
notes: No community name given in the listing; named from its opening words, "FOUR WOMEN."

name: A Woman's Place
notes: CLOSED: late 1981 to late 1982 (folded "in the past year" before the Dec 1982-Jan 1983 issue; exact date not given). "In the past year A Woman's Place (Athol, NY)... [has] folded" (LC Dec 1982; see observation 13). Founded September 1974, when seven women pooled their resources and purchased a former mountain resort (per LC Sept 1976).

name: Elwha River land
notes: No name given; the listing is a letter headed "DEAREST WOMYN:" (a greeting, not a name). Named from the Elwha River, which runs through the property. Owned by the gay community of Seattle (per LC Sept 1976).
